newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SHORT-COVERING HELPS SINGAPORE STOCKS BUCK KL FALL.
newsitem.headline: SHORT-COVERING HELPS SINGAPORE STOCKS BUCK KL FALL.

text.p: Singapore shares recovered a little on Tuesday morning after a recent sell-off as investors picked up a range of blue-chip stocks, dealers said.
The rally bucked a strong downward trend in the Kuala Lumpur stock market in Malaysia, which saw its blue-chip share index fall 1.87 percent in morning trade.
Few dealers expected the Singapore market to fall much further, but none predicted a significant short-term rally.
By 0430 GMT, the benchmark Straits Times Industrial Index (STII) was 9.24 points higher at 1,903.10. Total market volume was 107.7 million shares with 174 rises and 129 falls.
"Much of the selling yesterday was of foreign tranches by overseas funds and it was shorting. Now those positions are being covered back," said a broker with one major European bank.
On Monday, the 30-share STII dipped to four-year lows to end 2.58 percent, or 50.06 points, down at 1,893.86.
Dealers said there was a general perception that Singapore stocks were no longer expensive, but most investors still thought it might not yet be time to buy.
"Electronics stocks are already fairly valued, there are ongoing worries over the local property sector, and the foreign tranches of banking stocks are fairly valued," said one.
"Personally I think the market is going to be flat for a long time. I wouldn't see the STII beyond 2,200 points in the next year or year and a half," he added.
Dealers said a dip in the value of the Singapore dollar, which fell to a low of 1.5130 to the U.S. dollar from around 1.4850/70 early on Tuesday, had not affected the stock market.
The Singapore currency fell after comments by a finance official which dealers interpreted as leaving open the possibility of further exchange rate falls.
Top of the early stock market volume was venture capital firm Hotung Investment, which rose 4.5 cents to US$0.555 on its second day of trading.
Many of the more than 35 million shares traded in Hotung during the morning were crossed off the market.
